events.ai_basis: The proof in this note is entirely due to GPT 5.6 Sol Ultra and the writeup with Codex.

why: OpenAI's proof claims the whole statement: every bridgeless graph has a cycle double cover. The loopless restriction in the Lean statement does not narrow the human argument, since Oum's Theorem 1 allows loops, and a loop is itself a cycle that can be used twice. I counted it as digested, not unreviewed. Carmesin, a named matroid and graph researcher, publicly wrote 'yes, the proof is correct'. Oum (with a seminar) and Geelen each published a digested rewrite of the argument. Under F9 that clears the bar even without a journal; the Lean builds played no part in this call. On AI role, OpenAI's attribution sentence comes from secondary sources, but Oum's arXiv text independently confirms that the proof is due to GPT 5.6. That makes it generated. The expositions, the formalisations, Zhang's history note and the Máčajová structural reduction carry no new mathematics on the statement, so they are none. Oum's AI credit belongs to the OpenAI event, not to his exposition (F13). Kintali's independent claim is whole but unreviewed and doubtful. Ghanbari–Šámal bound the number of singular edges in an equivalent reformulation, where zero singular edges is the conjecture, so I read it as a bound rather than a variant. That was a close call, and it is moot beside the whole result. Pre-snapshot claims are withdrawn, carry acknowledged errors, or have no uptake at all.
doubts: The OpenAI PDF was never opened, so the exact attribution wording, including the Codex write-up credit, is unverified at source. Oum's quote corroborates the GPT credit. Carmesin's post did not show the details of his check. Dates conflict between 10 and 12 July 2026, which does not matter here. The Máčajová et al. date is year-only, but a received date of June 2024 puts it after the snapshot.
